one_liner: Tiny C99 FLAC decoder with no libc and no heap use; author claims about 25% faster than the flac CLI.
what_it_does: Decodes a FLAC byte stream into interleaved int32 samples through a resumable state machine: you call fx_flac_process() with any-sized input and output buffers (down to single bytes), it consumes what it can, reports bytes read and samples written, and returns at the end of metadata and after every frame. The decoder lives in one caller-supplied memory block sized by fx_flac_size(max_block_size, max_channels) (about 40 KiB for 48 kHz stereo Subset streams, 2-3 MiB for any stream), so it runs on bare metal and in WebAssembly. It is not an API drop-in for libFLAC: no callbacks, no seeking, no metadata beyond STREAMINFO, no frame-header access, decoder only.
how_it_is_fast: Mostly by doing less, not by clever kernels: there is no MD5 computation, no file or WAV output, no allocation and no metadata parsing beyond STREAMINFO. The hot loops are plain C: a 64-bit MSB-first bit buffer refilled one byte at a time, Rice residuals whose unary prefix is read one bit per call, CRC-8/CRC-16 updated per byte through a table-driven callback, and a generic int64-accumulator LPC restore loop for every order; no SIMD and no count-leading-zeros tricks. libFLAC's current decoder, by contrast, reads Rice blocks word-wise with count-leading-zeros (plus a BMI2 variant), updates CRC-16 over whole words and has order-specialised LPC restore with 32-bit accumulation when safe. A compile-time switch FX_FLAC_NO_CRC (off by default, under #if 0) drops all CRC checks, which the source says makes the decoder 'significantly faster'.
when_to_use: Microcontrollers, bare-metal firmware or WASM builds that must decode FLAC with no C runtime and no malloc (8.8 KiB of WebAssembly per the README).
Streaming playback where FLAC bytes arrive in arbitrary chunks (network, DMA buffers) and you want a push-style decoder with no callbacks.
16- or 24-bit, 1-8 channel Subset files, where the integration tests compare every sample against the flac reference decoder; 48 kHz stereo needs only about 40 KiB of decoder state.
Projects that want to vendor two source files (src/foxen-flac.c and src/foxen-flac.h) instead of building libFLAC.
when_not_to_use: As a desktop or server throughput choice: there are no published numbers against libFLAC's library API, FFmpeg or dr_flac, and the bit-at-a-time Rice loop is simpler than libFLAC's word-wise count-leading-zeros reader. The author calls the code 'not optimized' and says ARM6 performance is 'significantly worse'.

32-bit FLAC (written by FLAC 1.4.0 and later, defined in RFC 9639): sample-size code 7 maps to -1 in fx_flac_sample_sizes_, so every frame header is rejected, and 33-bit side channels cannot fit the int32 buffers. The README's 'Supports all FLAC features' predates 32-bit FLAC.
Seeking, cue sheets, tags, pictures or ReplayGain: none of these are implemented, and seeking is explicitly out of scope.
When you need integrity verification of the decoded audio: the STREAMINFO MD5 is exposed but never computed.
Proprietary static linking without LGPL obligations: the licence is LGPL-2.1-or-later (since March 2025), so vendoring the .c file into closed code brings relinking terms.

integration.form: source-drop (two files) or Meson-built static/shared library
integration.dependencies: none (only assert.h, stddef.h, stdint.h, stdbool.h); the FX_FLAC_ALLOC_* convenience macros call malloc
integration.min_toolchain: C99 compiler; Meson for the tests; MSVC 19.28 (Visual Studio 2019) fixes merged in PR #7; Emscripten for WASM
integration.platforms: any: x86_64, ARM (Arduino support merged Feb 2025), WebAssembly; plain C with no SIMD
integration.thread_safety: Per instance: one decoder decodes one stream at a time and has no global mutable state (only static const tables), so separate instances can run in separate threads.

gotchas: Output samples are left-justified to fill the whole int32 (decoded value shifted left by 32 minus bit depth); shift right by (32 - FLAC_KEY_SAMPLE_SIZE) to get native PCM.

Errors after the metadata are not reported: a CRC mismatch, a reserved value, or a frame whose block size or channel count exceeds what the instance was sized for makes the decoder silently resynchronise to the next frame, so an undersized FX_FLAC_ALLOC_SUBSET_FORMAT_DAT() instance drops audio without an error.

The integration test (test_flac_integration.c) only checks 16- and 24-bit files against flac -d and skips other bit depths with 'we're probably fine'; the runner covers the IETF flac-test-files subset/ directory but not uncommon/ (which holds the 32 bps, changing-bitdepth and 768 kHz files).

README build notes look stale: it says to add flac.c and flac.h (the files are src/foxen-flac.c/.h) and its emcc command names subprojects/libfoxenbitstream, whose code is now copied into foxen-flac.c.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Symphonia or rusty_flac when the target is C or C++ with no runtime and no heap (MCU, WASM, kernel-like code) and footprint matters more than speed; those Rust siblings publish measured decode-speed tables against FFmpeg, which libfoxenflac does not. go-flac is an encoder and does not compete.
verified_claims_summary: The only speed evidence is one 2018 README sentence: about 25% faster than the flac command-line decoder on x86_64, with no file, machine, compiler, flags, flac version (likely 1.3.2, the release current then) or timing method, and no harness in the repo. That baseline does different work: flac -d always enables MD5 checking (FLAC__stream_decoder_set_md5_checking(..., true) in src/flac/decode.c) and writes a WAV file, while libfoxenflac computes no MD5 and may or may not have had CRCs enabled (FX_FLAC_NO_CRC). So the figure compares a stripped decoder with a full CLI pipeline, not library against library.
status_note: Stale (last commit 2025-03-29, a README fix, after the Feb 2025 Arduino support PR and the March 2025 relicence), 84 stars and no open issues, but it is small, dependency-free and LGPL-2.1-or-later, so it is easy to vendor for embedded or WASM decoding as long as 32-bit FLAC is not needed.
